On this day in 1919, the Senate passed the 19th amendment giving women the right to vote - at a time when no women even served in the Senate.

Now, we vote in the halls of Congress. 

And I will continue to ensure that all citizens can exercise the fundamental right to vote.

“This program cannot simply be a public relations exercise that provides cover for the company to hike prices on families seeking COVID-19 vaccines.”

I pressed Moderna on its Patient Assistance Program & plan to hike up the price of its COVID vaccine. 

https://t.co/Z134Gyp3M6

Veterans deserve the best possible mental health and addiction care services. I introduced a bipartisan bill to assess the quality of care that veterans receive for mental and addiction health treatment from providers both in and outside the Department of Veterans Affairs.

NEW: Read my op-ed in STAT about the importance of reauthorizing the bipartisan SUPPORT Act — a critical effort in fighting the fentanyl crisis. 

https://t.co/psg9AvtwSZ

Heartbroken to hear that Captain Jack Casey of Dover was one of the Marines who died during a training exercise this week.

Captain Casey dedicated his life to our country & we will forever owe him a debt of gratitude for his service. My thoughts are with his family at this time.

Great to join @SecBecerra to discuss how we are increasing access to health care and standing up to Big Pharma to lower prescription drug costs. 

We also visited the Moms in Recovery program at @DartmouthHealth, which provides addiction treatment for pregnant and new moms. https://t.co/GrfuOzIJO5

After 34 years as an anesthesiologist, Dr. Bob Andelman of Portsmouth retrained & volunteered for 7 more years to provide addiction treatment to Granite Staters. 

His determination to help others is inspiring & I’m proud to recognize him as February’s Granite Stater of the Month

Join me in recognizing Rare Disease Day, raising awareness of people around the world living with a rare disease.

I’ll keep working to support those with rare diseases, including pushing for the bipartisan Safe Step Act that helps people access treatment & medication they need.

Great to see the new Veteran Wellness Center at @VAManchester and hear about the new resources available for veterans to help them take care of their mental health as well as their physical health. https://t.co/ejITLUd4R0

Today is National Fentanyl Awareness Day.

NH is far too familiar with the devastating impact of fentanyl – spreading awareness about this dangerous drug & making sure that Granite Staters are informed can help prevent overdoses & reduce the stigma of seeking addiction treatment.

I’ve heard from Granite Staters – especially young people – about the need to strengthen mental health care.
 
Although we have made important strides in recent years to support mental health treatment, including through the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, there is more to do.

Exciting news: NH is one of only 10 states to be selected for a federal program through the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act to get increased funding for community mental health clinics — this will significantly expand access to mental health & addiction treatment services.
Most Senate Republicans just voted against protecting access to IVF and fertility treatment, reinforcing the ongoing threat that extremists pose to reproductive health care.

New Hampshire remains on the cutting edge of innovation and discovery – @dartmouth is set to receive significant federal funding to develop technology that will improve prostate cancer surgery. 
 
This project will help advance cancer research & treatment.
https://t.co/XpvAowwjD6

As we mark International Overdose Awareness Day today, we all have a role to play in making sure that Granite Staters are informed about the dangers of fentanyl to prevent overdoses & reduce the stigma of seeking addiction treatment.

We have made strides in combating the devastating fentanyl crisis but there is much more work to be done.

I spoke to addiction medicine doctors from NH & across the country about how we can keep expanding access to the gold standard of treatment for those dealing with addiction. https://t.co/IWtffgRayE

Elon Musk is a textbook playground bully — pushing other people down just to feel important. 
https://t.co/DMIlJq9t0A
Today is Rare Disease Day, a day to recognize the millions living with rare diseases and the work that still needs to be done to ensure equitable access to treatment.

Medicaid helped Cheri Bryer get addiction treatment and go back to work. The Republican budget proposal would make major cuts to Medicaid, putting at risk the care that helped Cheri enter into recovery.
 
Cheri, thank you for joining me for tonight. https://t.co/PFM1uFtV5g

Medicaid is one of the strongest weapons we have in the fight against fentanyl through covering addiction treatment – but Congressional Republicans & the Trump Administration want to take Medicaid away from people. Read more on the new Joint Economic Committee – Minority report:

Yesterday I got a first-hand look at the addiction treatment and support that Elliot Hospital’s Center for Recovery Management provides for Granite Staters.

The Republican plan to gut Medicaid would be devastating to these patients who are working toward recovery. https://t.co/TCrdMcgnbY

NH has long fought the devastating impacts of the fentanyl crisis, including through medication-assisted treatment, the gold standard for treating opioid addiction.

We cannot allow the Trump Administration to gut Medicaid and take away access to MAT.
https://t.co/e6KWVn8sBb

Under the Republican budget bill, more than 43,000 Granite Staters would lose their health coverage.

This bill is unacceptable and I will keep working to stop it.

Congressional Republicans are pushing an amendment to their budget bill that ends Medicaid Expansion in NH and in states across the country, and 20 million people losing health coverage nationwide.
 
That's unacceptable, and I'm fighting to stop it.
 
https://t.co/YbA1Dy3ifW

Because President Trump and Republicans chose tax cuts for billionaires over tax cuts for working families in their budget bill, heath care premiums under the Affordable Care Act are set to spike for people across the country.

I visited Monadnock Community Hospital and heard about how these cuts will affect patients’ access to care.
